callers.note: twin caller pinned in open PR #3049; refreshes the snapshot, copies the published 312 bytes under the publish mutex to a stack buffer at rsp+0x20, unlocks, then calls the consumer
callers.setup: rdi = rsp (out string on the caller stack), rsi = rsp+0x20 (snapshot copy), rdx = *(owner+0x780) (chain link)

callers.note: larger dump routine; also calls the sibling formatter 0x5eedda0 (sites 0x5ef674d, 0x5ef712b) and the helper 0x5eebd00 (sites 0x5ef6736, 0x5ef6dfb, 0x5ef7064); its own body is not pinned here
callers.setup: rdi = rsp+0x110 (out string), rsi = rsp+0x2b0 (snapshot copy from subobject+0x28, subobject = *(r12+0x128)), rdx = *(r12+0x780) (chain link, r12 = the caller's first argument)

census.fmt_shared_note: the fmt helper's fourth caller 0x5eedac6 sits in the sibling formatter 0x5eedda0 (FDE 0x5eedda0..0x5eee30c); the elapsed helper's second caller 0x5ef841f sits in the sibling consumer 0x5ef8360
census.stored_qwords_note: the listed qwords are .rela.dyn addend fields, not data pointers: 0x10f978/0x15c568 are the addends of the two RELATIVE records for the walker (0x64cde20, 0x64ecf80), and 0x7048 is the addend of the RELATIVE record for the initializer (0x63f3830, the .init_array slot). No pinned routine has a stored qword outside .rela.dyn. (Correction: open PR #3049's stored_qwords for the walker read 0x110978/0x15d568; the correct virtual addresses under the PT_LOAD mapping, vaddr == file offset in the first LOAD segment, are 0x10f978/0x15c568.)

chain_walk.rule: compare the head link's slot +0x98 against the walker 0x5d4d490 (RELATIVE at 0x64ecf80); call the first mismatching link's slot +0x98 with (rdi = link), or the third link's slot unconditionally when the first two both match; the return is the slot_now value used for secs_since

cleanup.rule: on exception the fragment disposes the two fmt strings and destroys the ostringstream, checks the stack canary, and resumes unwinding via _Unwind_Resume; five landing pads enter it at 0x5eefd4a, 0x5eefd53, 0x5eefd5b, 0x5eefd7e and 0x5eefd89

corrections: snapshot +0x128 is the filler's FOURTH argument (rcx, the first slot +0x98 return V, stored at counter_lo before the filler call) -- NOT the chain head. Open PR #3049's records.json snapshot field +0x128 ('chain head value, the filler's third argument') is wrong: the filler prologue moves rcx to r15 and stores r15 at snapshot+0x128 (filler.txt 0x5eef386, 0x5eef4f2); the third argument rdx (chain head) is never stored into the snapshot. The +0x130 field is zeroed by the filler and overwritten later with the second slot return via 0x5eee560, as #3049 records.

elapsed.rule: hi = snapshot+0x130, lo = snapshot+0x128; return hi - lo when lo < hi, else hi (unsigned 64-bit)

entry_loop.bounds: counts at snapshot+0xb0..+0x120 (14 slots), values at snapshot+0x40..+0xb0, names from the table at 0x6503dc0 (32-byte std::string entries)
entry_loop.format: per non-zero count: " " + name + "(" + count + "," + fmt(value) + "," + portion + "%)"
entry_loop.portion: (double)value * 100.0 / (double)snapshot+0x00, printed with iostream default %g precision 6; a zero capacity gives inf (value > 0) or -nan (value == 0, the x86 DIVSD 0.0/0.0 indefinite QNaN)
entry_loop.skip_rule: a slot whose count is zero prints nothing (no name, no separators)

fmt.format: snprintf(buf, 20, "%.2f %s", x, suffix) at 0x4311e3; the result is returned as a std::string (SSO for <= 15 chars, heap via _M_create above that)
fmt.rule: x = (double)value (unsigned, via the sign-bit fixup); scale by 1/1024 with suffix KB, then MB, then GB while x >= 1024.0; TB is the last suffix and is used unconditionally after the fourth scaling

header.format: "Block cache " + name + " capacity: " + fmt(+0x00) + " usage: " + fmt(+0x08) + " table_size: " + u64(+0x10) + " occupancy: " + u64(+0x18) + " collections: " + u32(+0x120) + " last_copies: " + u32(+0x124) + " last_secs: " + ratio + " secs_since: " + secs + "\n" + "Block cache entry stats(count,size,portion):"
header.last_secs: ratio = (double)elapsed(+0x130, +0x128) / 1000000.0, printed with iostream default %g precision 6
header.secs_since: (slot_now - snapshot+0x130) as unsigned 64-bit (wraps), divided by 1,000,000 by the magic multiply (0x431bde82d7b634db, high word, shift 18); verified equal to unsigned // 1_000_000 on 200,010 values

render.expected:
Block cache test@0x1234#56 capacity: 1.00 MB usage: 512.00 KB table_size: 7 occupancy: 3 collections: 5 last_copies: 2 last_secs: 500 secs_since: 500
Block cache entry stats(count,size,portion): DataBlock(3,2.00 KB,0.195312%) FilterMetaBlock(5,1.00 MB,100%)

initializer.method: calls the std::string-from-const-char* helper 0x5effdd0 once per entry with (rdi = table + i*0x20, rsi = literal), then registers __cxa_atexit(destructor 0x5effea0, table, guard 0x64efa20); the table itself lives in .bss, so its contents exist only through this initializer, not in the file

sibling_table.consumer: not pinned; the sibling consumer 0x5ef8360 (FDE 0x5ef8360..0x5ef94ee, one direct call at 0x5ef96db) is the unexamined candidate
sibling_table.note: initialized by the same 0x5f007f0 function, immediately after our table (entries at 0x6503c00 + i*0x20)

not_claimed: what the owner, the subobject, or the snapshot fields denote beyond the pinned offsets
what the slot +0x98 handler computes (its return is treated here only as a counter/timestamp value)
what the slot +0x70/+0x78/+0x80/+0x88 producers compute (their results are used only as the printed capacity/usage/table_size/occupancy)
the exact throw-site mapping of the five landing pads (they jump into the shared cleanup fragment 0x5eefd4a..0x5eefd9a; the exception table was not decoded)
the bodies of the two callers beyond the pinned call-site windows
the sibling consumer 0x5ef8360, the sibling formatter 0x5eedda0, and the helper 0x5eebd00
the role-to-index function 0x5f00570..0x5f006ac immediately before the initializer cleanup (jump-table entries for indices 1..12, unexamined)

behaviour on a null chain link, a chain shorter than the walk needs, or a snapshot whose capacity is zero with a nonzero value (the model prints inf; the binary's stream would print inf the same way, but no binary run confirms it)
a runtime write to any relocated global after load (only the relocated values are pinned)

arguments: out std::string* in rdi (a caller-stack string; the twin caller passes rsp, the big dump caller passes rsp+0x110)
snapshot record* in rsi (the published snapshot copy: twin caller rsp+0x20, big dump caller rsp+0x2b0)
chain link* in rdx (twin caller *(owner+0x780), big dump caller *(r12+0x780))
routine.returns: nothing (void); *out is assigned the built text

snapshot.base_note: 312-byte published snapshot; the consumer reads the copy its caller made from the published base (owner-subobject +0x28, per open PR #3049)

fields.+0x00: capacity u64, slot +0x70 chain result, human-size formatted
fields.+0x08: usage u64, slot +0x78 chain result, human-size formatted
fields.+0x10: table_size u64, slot +0x88 result (0 when the slot is the identity 0x5d3ef80)
fields.+0x120: sequence u32, incremented on every fill (printed as collections)
fields.+0x124: no-progress counter u32, bumped when the progress check fails (printed as last_copies)
fields.+0x128: prev_value u64, the FIRST slot +0x98 return at fill time
fields.+0x130: last_value u64, the SECOND slot +0x98 return (last produced value)
fields.+0x18: occupancy u64, slot +0x80 result (-1 when the slot is the identity 0x5d3ef70); printed as an unsigned decimal, so -1 prints as 18446744073709551615
fields.+0x20: std::string name@0x<ptr>#<pid>, built by the filler 0x5eef380
fields.+0x40..+0xb0: values, 14 x u64, one per entry slot
fields.+0xb0..+0x120: counts, 14 x u64, one per entry slot; a zero count skips the line

tail.rule: after the entry loop the consumer inserts one '\n', then assigns the ostringstream content to *out (an _M_replace when the stream holds bytes, an _M_assign when it is empty); the destructor epilogue then disposes the stream and checks the canary
